descricao_original: A serosal membrane (serosa) lines internal body cavities, forming a parietal layer around the cavity’s inner wall and a visceral layer over organs protruding into the cavity. A serosa is composed of simple squamous epithelium (mesothelium) overlying a layer of connective tissue. Examples of serosal membranes are pleural, pericardial and peritoneal membranes identified in gross anatomy. 200x, 1000x
creditos_identificados: Image source: These images were taken of a slide from the University of Michigan collection.
